source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the wedding setting and kingdom comparison; virgins identified in vocabulary.
key_decisions.before: “Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
key_decisions.after: “Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: “Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the balanced division in a concise sentence.
key_decisions.before: Five of them were foolish and five were wise.
key_decisions.after: Five were foolish and five were wise.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

key_decisions.rationale: Makes the contrast compact without inserting extra oil into the main text.
key_decisions.before: The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take oil with them.
key_decisions.after: The foolish ones brought their lamps but no oil with them.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For when the foolish took their lamps, they took no oil with them,

key_decisions.rationale: Renders containers concretely while preserving the additional supply.
key_decisions.before: The wise ones took oil in containers along with their lamps.
key_decisions.after: The wise ones brought jars of oil along with their lamps.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: but the wise took flasks of oil with their lamps.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains all ten sleeping; does not turn foolishness into sleep alone.
key_decisions.before: When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
key_decisions.after: The bridegroom was delayed, and they all grew drowsy and fell asleep.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: As the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and slept.

key_decisions.rationale: Makes the sudden midnight cry natural without adding the absent comes verb.
key_decisions.before: But at midnight there was a shout: ‘Look, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’
key_decisions.after: At midnight a shout rang out: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him.’

key_decisions.rationale: Renders preparation broadly rather than specifying wick-trimming as certain.
key_decisions.before: Then all the bridesmaids got up and trimmed their lamps.
key_decisions.after: Then all the bridesmaids got up and put their lamps in order.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Then all those virgins rose and trimmed their lamps.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the request and immediate reason together.
key_decisions.before: The foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.’
key_decisions.after: The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And the foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the concern about sufficiency and direct instruction without adding a moral verdict.
key_decisions.before: But the wise answered, ‘There may not be enough for both us and you. Go instead to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’
key_decisions.after: But the wise ones answered, ‘There may not be enough for all of us. Go to the sellers and buy some for yourselves.’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But the wise answered, saying, ‘Since there will not be enough for us and for you, go rather to the dealers and buy for yourselves.’

key_decisions.rationale: Clarifies the simultaneous action and retains the shut door.
key_decisions.before: While they were going to buy it, the bridegroom came. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.
key_decisions.after: While they were away buying oil, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And while they were going to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.

key_decisions.rationale: Gives the repeated address audible dialogue without changing it to the narrator’s endorsement.
key_decisions.before: Later the other bridesmaids also came and said, ‘Lord, lord, open for us!’
key_decisions.after: Later the other bridesmaids came too. ‘Lord, lord,’ they said, ‘open the door for us!’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Afterward the other virgins came also, saying, ‘Lord, lord, open to us.’

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the denial of recognition and solemn introductory formula.
key_decisions.before: But he answered, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’
key_decisions.after: But he replied, ‘I tell you the truth: I do not know you.’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But he answered, ‘Truly, I say to you, I do not know you.’

key_decisions.rationale: Marks the return from parable dialogue to Jesus’ warning without adding a source-absent clause.
key_decisions.before: Therefore stay awake, because you know neither the day nor the hour.
key_decisions.after: “So stay awake, because you know neither the day nor the hour.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Therefore, stay awake, for you know neither the day nor the hour.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the large monetary unit and the source position of immediately, continuing into the next verse.
key_decisions.before: To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, each according to ability. Then he went away.
key_decisions.after: He gave one five talents, another two, and another one, each according to his ability. Then he left. At once,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his ability. Then he went away.

key_decisions.rationale: Joins at-once to the servant’s action across the verse boundary.
key_decisions.before: The one who received five talents went immediately, traded with them, and gained five more.
key_decisions.after: the servant who received five talents went to work with them and gained five more.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: He who had received the five talents went at once and traded with them, and he made five talents more.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the harsh assessment inside the servant’s speech and retains the agricultural images.
key_decisions.before: Then the one who had received one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew you were a harsh man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you scattered no seed.
key_decisions.after: Then the servant who had received one talent came forward. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘I knew you were a hard man. You reap where you have not sown and gather where you have not scattered seed.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: He also who had received the one talent came forward, saying, ‘Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you scattered no seed,

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves fear as the servant’s stated reason and the defensive return.
key_decisions.before: I was afraid, so I went and hid your talent in the ground. Look, you have what is yours.’
key_decisions.after: I was afraid, so I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here, you have what is yours.’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: so I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here you have what is yours.’

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the question echoing the servant’s accusation without certifying the accusation as narrator fact.
key_decisions.before: But his master answered, ‘Evil and lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I scattered no seed?
key_decisions.after: His master replied, ‘You wicked, lazy servant! You knew I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed?
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But his master answered him, ‘You wicked and slothful servant! You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I scattered no seed?

key_decisions.rationale: Retains brothers and sisters of mine without deciding the disputed referent in the translation.
key_decisions.before: The king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.’
key_decisions.after: The king will answer, ‘I tell you the truth: whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And the King will answer them, ‘Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’

key_decisions.rationale: Uses the same adjective for punishment and life and marks the return to narrative conclusion.
key_decisions.before: And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
key_decisions.after: And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
